root_cause.text: In `io_uring`’s `io_init_req()` the 128-byte SQE path for `IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED` incorrectly checked the logical SQ head (`ctx->cached_sq_head`) instead of the actual physical SQE slot (`sqe - ctx->sq_sqes`), allowing a user-controlled `sq_array` mapping to place a 128-byte request on the last SQE and trigger an out-of-bounds memcpy in `io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` with `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1`, and the CVE description says the old check was only correct for `NO_SQARRAY` rings while `sq_array` could remap a logical position to `sq_array[N] = sq_entries - 1`, causing a 64-byte read past the end of the SQE array.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mixed SQ request validation to reject 128-bit operations unless the SQE has a valid contiguous pair of entries available.
intent_record.what: In io_init_req(), the third condition in the validation check was changed from testing whether ctx->cached_sq_head is aligned to the SQ ring size mask to testing whether the current SQE pointer offset, (unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes), is greater than or equal to ctx->sq_entries - 1.
intent_record.how: This changes which SQE positions are considered valid for a mixed submission queue request that needs two contiguous entries. Instead of relying on the cached SQ head bit pattern, the code now directly checks the SQE's index within the SQ array and rejects requests when the entry would not have a following contiguous slot available.

grouping_result.intent: Fix mixed SQ request validation to reject 128-bit operations unless the SQE has a valid contiguous pair of entries available.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s intent matches the root cause: it fixes validation for mixed SQE requests so 128-byte operations are only allowed when a contiguous pair of SQEs exists, which addresses the same boundary-check flaw that led to the out-of-bounds memcpy.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix validation gate for mixed SQEs, and it is part of the check that failed to ensure the actual SQE slot had a contiguous pair available. The vulnerable logic continued past this point by relying on the wrong index source.

This is the directly vulnerable statement: it checks the logical SQ head rather than the physical SQE slot position, which allowed a user-controlled mapping to place a 128-byte request at the last SQE and reach an out-of-bounds memcpy.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the incorrect validation for the 128-byte SQE mixed path: it checks the logical SQ head (`ctx->cached_sq_head`) instead of the actual physical SQE slot, allowing a crafted `sq_array` mapping to place a 128-byte request on the last SQE and later trigger the out-of-bounds memcpy in `io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy()`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code already contains the safety check for mixed 128-byte SQEs: `if (def->is_128 && !(ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_SQE128)) { ... if (!(ctx->flags & IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED) || *left < 2 || !(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))) return io_init_fail_req(req, -EINVAL); ... }`. This commit introduces the fix by requiring `ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1)` to indicate a non-wrapping slot before accepting a 128-byte request on a mixed ring, and it also rejects impossible configuration via `io_uring_sanitise_params()` with `if ((flags & (IORING_SETUP_SQE128|IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED)) == (IORING_SETUP_SQE128|IORING_SETUP_SQE_MIXED)) return -EINVAL;`. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present here: there is no unchecked acceptance of a 128-byte SQE on the last physical SQE slot, and the code explicitly enforces contiguous space before proceeding.
